cells.tense: You are here with the pen, holding the whole shape and the thread to the other person at once.
cells.ask: Tell one person the whole pattern you see in their situation, including where the two of you differ, and stop there.
cells.core:
You can feel what someone is carrying without it taking over the room. The whole picture stays in view, theirs and yours together, and the warmth doesn't blur it. Plenty of people get one half of that: clear sight that runs cold, or warmth that loses the thread. Doing both at once is why what you notice tends to be right.

That steadiness isn't free. Staying in real contact without folding into anyone takes holding, and lately you're gripping a little harder than the moment asks. You don't have to prop up the room to stay close to it. Try saying the whole of what you see to one person and letting that be enough — no fixing, no follow-through. Fortitude here means bearing the moment without forcing it. The closeness survives it. It usually gets better.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the whole picture and stay close to people at the same time.
cells.verb: Feeling with another without losing where you end
cells.place: Standing outside the pattern while still inside it, seeing how the pieces fit

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future in which their weight becomes yours, hauling a load that has not arrived.
cells.ask: Take one thing you're carrying on someone else's behalf and put it down for a day, without announcing it.
cells.core:
You're running ahead of people. Their feeling shows up and you've already picked it up, already arranged your day around something they haven't asked you for. What should stay their shape becomes yours to hold, and the line between their state and yours goes thin. Being close isn't the same as having no line at all.

Gripping this hard isn't strength. It's the same pressure that turns holding into crushing. Something small needs to end here, and you're allowed to let it: one weight, handed back or simply set down where it sits. What you lose is the hauling around. What stays is the person, and they were not the weight.

cells.tense: You have stayed at the surface with people for a while, and it has held, and little has shifted.
cells.ask: Open one conversation this week past where it usually stops, with one true sentence about what you actually think.
cells.core:
You can read a whole situation and you keep the reading to yourself. The conversations stay easy, the tone of them stays mild, and mild has become the ceiling. You'd call it calm. It's closer to a room you stopped entering, and you've gotten good at standing in the hallway.

What's gone quiet isn't your eye for people. It's that feeling doesn't get rung up, so it doesn't answer. Don't push warmth into the flat place — that doesn't work. Steady yourself first, then say one true thing to one person, this week, and let the conversation go where it goes. One real sentence is enough to break the streak. You don't owe anyone more than that today.

cells.tense: You are already reading the whole shape and acting on it, while calling none of it care.
cells.ask: Pick one recent thing you did that looked like care and tell the person you did it for, in one sentence.
cells.core:
You notice what a person needs and you move. You take the longer route because it's kinder, and then you file it under errands. Nothing gets named on the way out, so from where you stand it reads as ordinary — logistics, a favor, no big deal. The softer thing comes through in what you do, not in what you report feeling.

Your eye for the whole pattern is what runs it. You catch a person's situation the way you'd catch a shift in the light, and then you act before you've decided it counts. Naming one of those moves doesn't make it soft. It puts it where you can see it, which is the only place it can grow into something you feel.
cells.sheetLine: Your care comes out in what you do, not in what you feel.

attempts.check: The record does not say the person's surface connection is a defense or that anything in their history made feeling unsafe — so the Too Little cell locates the numbness but states nothing about when, how, or with whom it began, and does not say the disconnection was ever a decision. A reader could reasonably say the surface-ness is preference, not numbness, or that they simply haven't met anyone worth going deep with; every cell is written so that 'no, that isn't what's happening' still leaves a usable act. The asks survive that objection because they are observation and one honest act, not repairs — naming what's already recognized, letting one thing stay theirs, being wrong in front of one person, telling one person which way you're leaning — none of them depends on my read being correct. The sentence that serves the writer is 'Others feel your care — people know it' in the Unacknowledged cell, which would tell the person what they're missing and risks flattering a warm abstraction; it's cut back to a plain report of what reaches others and swapped for 'the softer thing comes out in what you do, not in what you feel,' keeping the fact without the sentiment.
